item.title: Bombshell report details rift between Bayern Munich, Jamal Musiala’s management
item.description: (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images An explosive report from German outlet Stern (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) details the growing schism between Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management. If true, Bayern Munich’s decision to go public and en gage in this fracas through the media sti ll loo ks bad, though there do appear to be issues with transparency and understanding from both sides, along with a total lack of a plan for how to move forward. The report goes back to last season and points to Musiala having a seizure on April 7, the day Bayern Munich played Real Madrid in the Champions League: A @sternde team conducted intensive research into the Jamal Musiala case in recent weeks and spoke with numerous people close to the club. The emerging picture revealed a veritable power struggle between the club’s management and Musiala’s representatives, involving new information, mistrust, and suspicion Here are the main points/results of the investigation: -Musiala suffered a lapse four days before his return to training, which was initially kept from the public by Bayern’s sporting management and the player’s management. The club’s higher ups only learned of it later in the week and were annoyed -Musiala also suffered an absence seizure on the morning of the Real Madrid game on April 7th while in a Madrid hotel. He was later subbed on in the game. What Musiala’s entourage considers a normal and manageable part of everyday life for someone with a neurological dysfunction is said to have infuriated some of the club’s bosses – because they were allegedly not informed about the player’s lapses at all, or only informed later -Some of the bosses now believe that the player’s management is withholding something crucial from them, that something is being covered up, and that the player’s health could be in a worse state than they are being told -@sternde confronted Jamal Musiala’s management with these and other questions. The player’s representatives stated that they would not comment on individual medical incidents. The agency added that they maintain a good and constructive dialogue with Bayern’s sporting management. FC Bayern also declined to comment for legal reasons -Bayern bosses are concerned that Musiala is allowed to choose his own doctors, while the club is kept in the dark. The concern also includes the fact that Musiala’s camp explicitly negotiated a much longer period of sick pay than usual, which seemed dubious given the illness – because the contract was signed before the diagnosis was made public. The bosses are now suspecting that they may have been taken advantage of Health aside, the massive financial stake in the player (potential €150 million total package through 2030) has the club concerned. item.title: What we know about the 2035 UK Women's World Cup – and the questions that remain
item.description: It’s official: the 2035 Women’s World Cup belongs to the United Kingdom . This shouldn’t come as a surprise. England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland were the only bidders for the tournament, with the decision confirmed at a special FIFA meeting on Monday. Even so, the announcement is significant. The UK has not hosted a senior World Cup, men’s or women’s, since England staged (and won) the men’s edition in 1966. Nine years can feel like a long way away and, in the history of Women’s World Cup bidding rights, it is. Never before has a host nation for the women’s tournament been confirmed this far in advance. For the UK, it means time is both on the four home nations’ side and of the essence. The bid was clear in its expectations and ambitions: 104 matches, 48 teams, a potential 22 stadiums, 16 host cities, 4.5 million fans attending and 3.5 billion watching from their televisions around the globe. But what other ambitions does the UK have and what unknowns remain? The Athletic outlines the main talking points below. What do we know about dates and venues? Despite being the only bidders in the process, there are still many unknowns. Exact dates are to be confirmed, though we do know the tournament will consist of 104 matches over 39 days, with 48 teams competing (16 more than will be involved in next summer’s World Cup in Brazil). In the UK’s official bid, 19 venues were definitively included, the majority (14) of which are in England, with two from both Wales and Scotland and one in Northern Ireland. England’s venues are: Villa Park (Birmingham), the Amex (Brighton), Ashton Gate (Bristol), Elland Road (Leeds), Hill Dickinson Stadium (Liverpool), Emirates Stadium (London), Selhurst Park (London), Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (London), Wembley (London), Etihad Stadium (Manchester), St James’ Park (Newcastle), the City Ground (Nottingham), the Stadium of Light (Sunderland), and Old Trafford (Manchester). The Scotland venues are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road. Wales’ stadiums are Cardiff City Stadium and the Principality Stadium, both in Cardiff, while Northern Ireland’s Windsor Park (Belfast) is also included. Wembley is currently the only venue listed as a potential host for the competition’s final. However, that doesn’t mean other stadiums cannot still be a potential host venue — or even a venue for the final. In fact, Birmingham City’s new ground, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and any new Chelsea stadium can also be in the mix. No timeframe for when the stadiums must be finished has been provided, with such deadlines falling under FIFA’s jurisdiction, according to the Football Association’s director of women’s football, Sue Day. Day said the choice of stadiums was a reflection of the anticipated attendance at matches both from FIFA and the host nations themselves. item.title: Dodgers notes – is it good Tarik Skubal signed elsewhere?
item.description: The biggest domino to fall this offseason fell Sunday, as Tarik Skubal signed with the New York Mets for 9 years, $450 million. The Los Angeles Dodgers did not even get to the point where they offered their playoffs starter a contract, as they were unwilling to go the number of years that Skubal was looking for. In her column on Monday, Mirjam Swanson of the L.A. Times argues that it is a good thing that the Dodgers missed out on the two-time Cy Young winner. As Swanson points out, Skubal is 30 years old and has already had three elbow surgeries. He will be 38 when his contract ends. And, as Swanson also pointed out, the Dodgers have eight starting pitchers without Skubal. They also have a stacked farm system should they feel the need to go out and trade for a starter at the deadline (should there be a season of which to have a deadline). Jim Swanson of the OC Register also ponders if its good that the Dodgers did not sign Skubal. He doesn’t beat around the bush, starting off by saying that the contract the Mets gave Skubal will not age well, because of the age of Skubal and his past injuries. Before this, Yoshinobu Yamamoto had the biggest contract for a pitcher, and as Swanson points out, he has more than lived up to his contact, in part bringing two World Series to the Dodgers, one of which he was the World Series MVP. Time will tell if this was a good move by Mets owner Steve Cohen or just be another one of his huge contracts that didn’t quite pan out. At least we know it’s not just the Dodgers “ruining baseball”.

item.title: When will the Red Sox pay someone $400M?
item.description: Boston, MA - October 5: Boston Red Sox manager Chad Tracy, chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and president Sam Kennedy attend an end-of-season press conference on October 5, 2026. (Photo by David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images Major League Baseball could be undergoing some major changes over the next few months… I’d love to tell you folks that things are going to get figured out, but lying isn’t my bag and it looks extremely likely that we are just days away from a work stoppage, as the collective bargaining agreement between the MLBPA and the owners is set to expire on on Dec. 1. MLB commissioner Rob Manfred offered up a disheartening outlook on the situation last Wednesday, when he told reporters that the owners are adamant about instituting a salary cap that has been strongly opposed by the players’ union. MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer is being tasked with stopping the biggest fundamental change to the sport in decades, while also looking to impose changes that will allow players earlier freedom as the union is proposing expanded rosters, guidelines to protect against service time manipulation, and a soft floor that penalizes teams who don’t spend a certain amount. If you’re one of the millionaires, let me be the first to tell you that you’re not going to get everything you want. If you’re one of the billionaires, let me start by telling you to pound sand and continue by telling you that you, too, won’t be getting everything that you desire. I don’t have any clue as to what’s going to happen, but one question that has popped up in the final days of the current collective bargaining agreement is: How long it will take to see someone sign a $400 million deal with the Boston Red Sox. The New York Mets just handed out the fifth such contract in the history of the sport, when they agreed to terms with Tarik Skubal on Sunday. His new $450 million deal puts him in the same conversation as new teammate Juan Soto ($765M), old teammate Shohei Ohtani ($700M), Vladimir Guerrero Jr. ($500M), and Mike Trout ($426M). If a salary cap/floor is implemented, we could see the length of time between the most recent deal of that magnitude and the next deal of that magnitude greatly increase, but how does that impact the folks down at Four Jersey Street? The Red Sox don’t exactly seem eager to hand out $400 million, but they are just a few years removed from handing out $313 million to Rafael Devers. They were also said to be willing to pay an exorbitant amount of money to sign Soto, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Alex Bregman, Pete Alonso and other big name free agents in recent years. I don’t want to give them credit for ultimately cheaping out, but you would have to imagine there are circumstances that could see them eventually open up the pocket book — whether that be inflation, the presence of a salary cap and floor, or another once-in-a-lifetime talent who comes available and is willing to join them. item.title: How Chiefs Are Preparing For Bills Star Josh Allen
item.description: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen and Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes meet after an NFL game on Dec. 10, 2023. (AP Photo/Ed Zurga) Copyright 2023 The Associated Press. All Rights Reserved The 6-5, 237-pound Josh Allen is a unique weapon who can make big plays with his arms or legs. But the Buffalo Bills quarterback did not have a single rushing attempt during Sunday’s victory against the Miami Dolphins. “That’s a setup,” Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo said. “They’ll have a good number of designed quarterback runs … We’re certainly going to be focused on quarterback runs and what he can do with the ball in his hands.” The Thanksgiving night game is setting up as another classic between two AFC heavyweights. Since Allen and Patrick Mahomes have become the starting quarterbacks for their respective teams, the Bills and Chiefs have met annually — and often times more than once — in every year, beginning in 2020. They are two of the best players in the NFL and are paid like it. In terms of contract value, Mahomes ranks first with a $504.75 million contract, and Allen is second with $330 million. But to prepare for Allen, the Chiefs used to turn to one of its bargain players on the practice squad. Quarterback Chris Oladokun used to impersonate mobile quarterbacks like Allen and Jalen Hurts, but Oladokun is now playing in the CFL. The Chiefs have not confirmed this, but one would think they have Justin Fields mimic Allen during their truncated week of practice. The athletic, 6-3, 227-pound Fields even ran for 1,143 yards and eight touchdowns during his second year in the NFL. The Allen-Mahomes Rivalry Since the Chiefs began playing against Allen, starting in 2020, Spagnuolo said Allen has developed into a more cerebral quarterback. And the Bills have won five consecutive regular-season meetings between the teams. They won during the 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022 and 2021 regular seasons, and the Chiefs won in the 2020 regular season. “He’s got this competitive nature about him,” Spagnuolo said, “where they’re going to somehow, someway will their team to win.” Though Allen has willed the Bills to win the regular-season contests between the teams, the rub is that the Chiefs have dominated the more important playoff games. The Chiefs are 4-0 against the Bills in the playoffs during The Mahomes Era, having won playoffs games after the 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2024 regular seasons. item.title: Dolphins Defense Holds Ground While Offense Falters In Buffalo
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The team looked like a 1-8 squad for large parts of the afternoon, struggling to move the ball against a tough opponent. Even with a backup quarterback under center and an entire defensive line missing, the unit showed some fight before the offense gave up on them. According to Dolphins Talk , “You can’t expect that unit to do that for all 4 quarters without eventually cracking, especially when the offense is giving you no help, but kudos to Hafley for having the defense ready to play.” Stock Up for the Defense Chop Robinson has really improved his run game, showing he can stop the run while still rushing the passer. The linebacker is now a true four-down player who isn’t a liability against the run, which is a massive upgrade for the front seven. Jacob Rodriguez recorded double-digit tackles and made a big interception right before halftime to keep the score down. These players deserve credit for keeping the Dolphins in the game when the offense could not find a rhythm. The special teams unit, however, has been bad all year, and that trend continued on Sunday. Additionally, Chris Bell dropped a ball that hit him in the hands in the first half, a mistake that killed a potential drive. The source notes that this drop was critical because the offense needed every yard it could get. That is inexcusable, and the excuse “well, he is a rookie” won’t work in that situation. Stock Down for the Offense In the past 3 weeks, Caleb Douglas has dropped far too many passes, and this habit is now hurting the team’s chances to win close games. These drops are either bad luck or a failure of focus that the coaching staff must address immediately. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 29, 1 p.m. ET: New York Jets at Miami Dolphins, Hard Rock Stadium.

item.title: Jayden Daniels may have cost Stefon Diggs a huge $250K bonus with Commanders snub
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs did not see eye to eye during the Washington Commanders’ win over the Cincinnati Bengals. Diggs was seen on camera chastising Daniels for not passing the ball to him when he was making runs that could have helped the Commanders advance the ball or even score touchdowns. The speech didn’t have much of an impact, as Daniels was unable to find Diggs in the right spots when needed, and in doing so, cost the WR a sizeable bonus. Stefon Diggs missed out on $250K bonus against Cincinnati Bengals thanks to Jayden Daniels Interestingly, prior to the game, one NFL news account reported that Stefon Diggs would have triggered a bonus clause in his Washington Commanders contract with two or more touchdowns against the Cincinnati Bengals. With $250K on the line, Diggs’ frustration with Daniels makes a lot more sense, as he saw the young QB’s failure as an act that was costing him a large sum of money. During the win against the Bengals, Diggs only had four receptions across six targets, receiving for only 45 yards. Compare this to WR Antonio Williams, whom Daniels found nine times across 11 attempts, allowing him to receive for 122 yards, and Diggs’ frustration becomes all the more justified. If it is even possible to give Diggs any consolation, Daniels failed to find any of his receivers on the night to throw for touchdowns, with the Commanders winning because of their success from field goal range. Diggs had a clause in his contract to receive a $250K incentive bonus for five or more touchdowns this season, a mark he has already hit. If he manages to catch two or more touchdowns in his next game, he will receive the second portion of that incentive bonus worth $250K, thus bringing his earnings through incentives to $500K for the season. item.title: Jamie Carragher says Chelsea have ‘no chance of achieving anything’ with current defence
item.description: Jamie Carragher has warned Chelsea they have “got absolutely no chance of achieving anything” with their current defensive options as he likened Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill to “kids”. Xabi Alonso ’s side were thumped 4-1 at home by rivals Leeds on Saturday and have conceded 20 goals in 11 Premier League games this season. With £52m summer signing Maxence Lacroix sidelined with a hamstring injury, Fofana and Colwill have been Alonso’s centre-back pairing for the Blues’ last three matches. Former Liverpool defender Carragher delivered a scathing assessment as he analysed Leeds’ equaliser, scored by Noah Okafor. “That is as bad as it gets in terms of conceding a goal in the Premier League,” Carragher said on Sky Sports’ Monday Night Football. “You feel like you’re seeing kids playing in a men’s game. That’s the best way to describe it.” Only the bottom two, Crystal Palace and Manchester United, and promoted sides Ipswich and Coventry have worse defensive records than Chelsea. The Blues have lost three of their last four top-flight matches and are already 12 points adrift of leaders Arsenal and five behind fourth-placed Liverpool in the race for Champions League qualification. Levi Colwill (left) has struggled to get back to form since returning from injury (Reuters) “Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don’t change it in January, they’re going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League,” said Carragher. “Lacroix is a decent player, that’s a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything.” Chelsea were booed off by the home supporters who remained at Stamford Bridge after their thrashing by Leeds. The heavy defeat followed a 2-0 home loss to London rivals Tottenham and a 1-0 reverse at Sunderland , either side of a 2-0 victory over Manchester United . Xabi Alonso's side were booed off after defeat to Leeds (Getty) “Colwill at Sunderland against (Brian) Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time,” said Carragher. “Fofana’s performance against Manchester United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you’ll see from a centre-back this season. “As a partnership, this will never work because they’re not physical enough and there’s no real leader there.” Frenchman Fofana, 25, joined Chelsea in a £75m deal from Leicester in 2022, while 23-year-old Colwill came through the club’s academy and has been capped five times by England. “It almost feels like you’ve got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well,” added Carragher. Eighth-placed Chelsea return to action away to Nottingham Forest on Friday evening.

item.title: Dolphins considering offensive line change as Austin Jackson struggles
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 30: Austin Jackson #73 of the Miami Dolphins takes the field prior to a game against the New Orleans Saints at Hard Rock Stadium on November 30, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Miami Dolphins offensive tackle Austin Jackson has struggled this season. While the primary concern with Jackson since Miami selected him in the first round of the 2020 NFL Draft has been his availability, his on-field play in 2026 has not been up to standard. On Sunday, against the Buffalo Bills, edge rusher Greg Rousseau routinely ran through Jackson to pressure quarterback Kyle McCord. It was not a highlight day for Jackson, but, this season, there have been more bad days than good ones. On Monday, head coach Jeff Hafley admitted a change could be coming to the offensive line as Jackson’s struggles continue. “Yeah, I would say we’ll look at the offensive line hard this week,” Hafley told the South Florida media. “We sat down this morning, we’re going to do more this afternoon, and we’ll look at everything to see what we need to do to help him more and what we need to do overall. Like I said to you guys yesterday, we’ll take a look at what we can do better to help, and then we’ll take a look at what we can do overall to play better on offense. So I would say that with all the positions.” Hafley was then asked if the Dolphins are considering moving rookie guard Kadyen Proctor out to right tackle to replace Jackson. The coach responded, “I would say conversations have been had, because there’s a lot of conversations and I say that to be honest with you. As of right now, I don’t see him playing tackle this week. So yeah, that’s how I’d answer your question.” Hafley does not see Proctor playing tackle this week. He did not say he does not see Proctor playing tackle in a couple of weeks or later in the season. Proctor was Miami’s first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft and played tackle at Alabama. Jackson is entering the final year of his contract and is not expected to re-sign with Miami; he will hit the free-agent market and likely move to a new team next year. It has been assumed that Proctor would move out to right tackle for 2027, replacing Austin while Miami looks for a new starting left guard. Hafley’s comments suggest the Dolphins could make that move this year, rather than waiting until next season. If the Dolphins want to keep Proctor at guard this season, where he has been playing well, they could look to Chukwuebuka Godrick to slide into the starting lineup as a replacement for Jackson. They would then have the option of using the offseason to prepare Proctor for the move for 2027. Jackson is not the only player on the line who could be headed toward the bench. item.title: Emmanuel Sanders predicts how many Super Bowls the 49ers will win in the next 10 years
item.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Former Super Bowl champion Emmanuel Sanders reveals how many Super Bowls he thinks the San Francisco 49ers will win in the foreseeable future. The San Francisco 49ers are tied with the Buffalo Bills for the best record in the NFL through 10 games. The team has lost just once, and they look like a serious Super Bowl contender yet again. Under head coach Kyle Shanahan, the Niners have made it all the way twice (in 2019 and 2023), but lost against the Kansas City Chiefs on both occasions. Quarterback Brock Purdy has been putting together an MVP campaign. The 26-year-old has a completion rate of 71 percent, has 23 touchdowns on the year to just five interceptions, and has an excellent 118.2 passer rating. His play and the team’s success have some former stars feeling good about the current iteration of the Niners. Emmanuel Sanders says San Francisco 49ers could win ‘two or three Super Bowls’ in 10 years Since Shanahan took over, the Niners have made the playoffs in five out of nine seasons. They have proven to be perennially dangerous, with only injuries causing their downfall in recent years. And while they aren’t over the hump yet, there is no reason to believe they won’t do it soon. Former 49ers star Emmanuel Sanders is a believer. He highlighted the duo of Purdy and Shanahan while expressing his confidence in the team’s ability to win a lot in the coming seasons. “Kyle Shanahan is a bad boy, you know, and it’s the reason why I sit back and say he’s a future Hall of Fame coach,” Sanders said. “Hey, look, I’m even jumping in. I think him and Purdy are going to win not just one, but multiple Super Bowls together, because Purdy is still young. Like I wouldn’t be surprised if they win two or three Super Bowls in the next 10 years with how they’re looking you know?” This is certainly a bold prediction, there are never any guarantees in the NFL. San Francisco has consistently fielded talented rosters in the 2020s, but it is yet to lead to Super Bowl success. If they do actually manage to win two or three in the next decade, it would be a huge success for Shanahan and the franchise. item.title: Barcelona summer signing has special memories of Azerbaijan ahead of Sabah encounter
item.description: Barcelona summer signing has special memories of Azerbaijan ahead of Sabah encounter Barcelona travel to Azerbaijan without Lamine Yamal for Wednesday’s Champions League meeting with Sabah, but Hansi Flick has another attacker with outstanding memories of playing in Baku. As such, Anthony Gordon returns to the city where he scored four goals in a remarkable European performance for Newcastle United earlier this year. Since joining Barcelona, Gordon has recorded three goals and five assists in 16 matches across all competitions. However, his previous Champions League campaign showed the attacking threat that convinced Barcelona to bring him to the club. Notably, Gordon scored an impressive 10 goals in 12 appearances in the competition last season, including four in a single match against Qarabag. Gordon’s unforgettable four-goal performance in Baku On February 18, 2026, Newcastle travelled to Azerbaijan for the first leg of their Champions League knockout play-off against Qarabag. Gordon produced one of the most extraordinary individual performances of the campaign, scoring four times as the English side secured a 6-1 victory. His goals arrived in the third, 32nd, 33rd and the first-half stoppage time. The final two included a penalty after he was brought down by goalkeeper Mateusz Kochalski, while his earlier strikes helped Newcastle establish an overwhelming advantage before half-time. The match took place at the Tofiq Bahramov Republican Stadium, in front of 28,861 spectators, where Gordon was substituted in the 68th minute after completing his four-goal haul. As such, Newcastle eventually progressed with a 9-3 aggregate victory. Barcelona face a different challenge against Sabah Anthony Gordon has special memories of playing in Azerbaijan. (Photo by Aziz Karimov/Getty Images) This time, Gordon returns to Baku wearing Barcelona colours, but the challenge will be different. Flick’s side will face Sabah at the Baku Olympic Stadium, which has a listed capacity of 69,870, rather than the venue where Gordon produced his memorable display. Barcelona will also be without Yamal , who is unavailable because of right-ankle discomfort. His absence leaves Flick with fewer options in attack and increases the importance of Gordon’s contribution on the left. The Englishman could benefit from the opportunity to start after being used from the bench against Villarreal. Hence, it can be argued that Gordon is a strong candidate to occupy the left wing, while Karim Adeyemi could operate on the right, and Raphinha could continue playing centrally.

item.description: The Oregon football team has put itself in position to potentially qualify for the Big Ten Championship game after seemingly being out of the mix of the College Football Playoff a month ago. With a date against rival Washington Nov. 28 at Autzen Stadium , the Ducks (8-3, 6-2 Big Ten) would do themselves a massive favor with a win. The Huskies (7-4, 4-4) have won four of their last five games, including a major upset of defending national champion Indiana last Saturday in Seattle. "Obviously an exciting opportunity for us this weekend," coach Dan Lanning said. "Get an opportunity to play a rival and our seniors' last game here potentially in Autzen. So exciting for them, especially for the guys that have given so much to this program and been involved for as long as they have. And for it to be a game like this one is a special opportunity for us." Watch Oregon football on Peacock Oregon vs. Washington scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: Both the Ducks and Huskies have prolific passing attacks, ranking in the top 20 nationally, but where Oregon has a significant advantage is on the ground. UW ranks third-worst in Power Four football in rushing yards per game, totaling just over 100 yards. The Huskies have been snakebit at running back with injuries all year. But former Oregon Duck Jayden Limar has come on strong in recent weeks for UW, which ran for nearly 200 yards against Indiana's top-rated rush defense last week. The Ducks average nearly 40 yards more per game on the ground and could really command Saturday's game in the trenches. Why Washington has an advantage: Oregon leads Washington in just about every statistical category, though not overwhelmingly. The Huskies are slightly better on special teams, averaging 2 yards more per punt and hitting field goals at a higher rate. But where Washington is significantly better is in protecting the ball, outside of interceptions. Oregon has lost 10 fumbles this season to Washington's four, though the Ducks have yet to put the ball on the ground in the month of November. item.title: Tristan Thompson gives his exact timeline for when Bitcoin will reach $1 million
item.description: Photo By Sam Barnes/Sportsfile for Web Summit Qatar via Getty Images Former NBA champion Tristan Thompson is making a bold bet on crypto and Bitcoin. Just weeks ago, crypto bulls were calling for fresh all-time highs, yet Bitcoin has dropped roughly 20 percent this month, hitting a two-year low around $55,250. Caught up in a wider stock market sell-off and heavy ETF outflows, the token just hasn’t been able to shake off the panic. Even Monday’s huge rebound in tech stocks, sparked when Nvidia suddenly brought Jensen Huang back as CEO, only gave Bitcoin a brief pop toward $64,500 before it slid right back down. However, Tristan Thompson is slightly more optimistic about the future movement of Bitcoin, predicting that we could see it reach $1 million within five years. Speaking on the 2a1c show, he said: “I think we get back to $90K by spring. I think we could see a new all-time high end of 2027. And then I think every year it’ll just keep growing. “Bitcoin in the last 14 years has done about 70% appreciation. Obviously that number will come down as more gets accumulated. I think within five years we’ll see a million dollars.” NBA players keep wading deeper into crypto and stocks. Kyle Kuzma even sparked plenty of debate recently by telling millennials to put their cash into the stock market instead of real estate, showing athletes aren’t just collecting paychecks anymore, they’re handing out financial advice online. item.description: Jose Valenzuela speaks with Ring Magazine about what he anticipates will be a mandatory WBA title fight against Floyd Schofield early next year and his inability to secure a fight against Shakur Stevenson under Zuffa’s banner. Check out some of what he had to say with the full video interview below. Valenzuela on his plans for the coming year “Huge 2027. I’m very excited going into this year and we’re kicking it off right with the WBA title shot versus Floyd Schofield. The WBA mandated it so now we just got to get through getting a deal for the both of us and getting this fight going the first quarter of the year. “He’s been well developed by his promotion company and you got me, who’s a real fighter, comes to win, comes for the knockout, comes with mean intentions and I got a lot of experience under my belt. I also think I have abilities that he hasn’t seen before. His opponents have been handpicked out for him, but this time he’s going to meet somebody 5’10, can do a lot, can box, can fight on the inside. I come conditioned as well, I come prepared. So, it’s going to be a hell of a fight. “I’m focused on Kid Austin, on him and his abilities and I know what he does well and what he doesn’t. So, that’s kind of what I focus on…I think they’re in for a rude awakening when the fight comes.” On Shakur Stevenson dismissing a fight against him “I thought he was weak for that. On Twitter he’ll engage with everybody…I thought it was interesting he’d rather leave a great deal on the table that he had with Zuffa and now I guess he’s fighting Ashton Sylve…He maybe doesn’t want a dangerous fight right now. “He just wants to box comfortably, he doesn’t want to feel no pressure and that’s what I do. item.title: The Lions Are About to Ask the Bears a Question the Saints Couldn’t
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The New Orleans Saints found out what happens when the Chicago Bears get to rush the passer with a lead. Jared Goff and the Detroit Lions are about to find out, too. The more interesting question is whether the Bears can create those same conditions against one of the NFL’s most dangerous offenses. Chicago’s defense overwhelmed New Orleans for long stretches Sunday, collecting six sacks and two takeaways in a 21-13 victory. Jeffery Simmons had three sacks. Montez Sweat produced a safety. Clark Phillips III forced a fumble that set up a touchdown. It was the kind of performance that makes the Bears look capable of winning even when Caleb Williams and the offense are having an uneven afternoon. Thursday will demand more. Detroit enters the Thanksgiving matchup at 8-2, tied with Chicago. The Lions have a quarterback who understands their offense, a dangerous group of receivers, an outstanding offensive line and a running back who can turn one missed assignment into a much larger problem. For defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, the challenge begins before Goff ever drops back. A different kind of test up front Nov 15, 2026; Munich, DEU; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) celebrates after a touchdown against the New England Patriots at the 2026 NFL Munich Game at Allianz Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Jahmyr Gibbs gives the Lions a threat who can hurt a defense as both a runner and receiver. He leads the league with 17 runs of at least 15 yards. Allen called him a “home-run threat every time he touches the ball” and said stopping him will require all 11 defenders. That is relevant because two of New Orleans’ biggest plays exposed gaps in an otherwise productive defensive performance. Travis Etienne broke a 46-yard run, and quarterback Tyler Shough escaped for a 30-yard scramble. Both drives produced points. Allen said Monday that the Bears generally handled the Saints’ running game well, while acknowledging mistakes on those explosive gains. Against Detroit, the cost of a similar lapse could rise quickly. Chicago has allowed only 94 rushing yards per game, seventh-fewest in the league, but opponents have averaged 4.5 yards per carry. The Bears have faced relatively few rushing attempts in part because they have played from ahead throughout their five-game winning streak. That combination makes Thursday a useful test. Can the Bears control Gibbs often enough to put Detroit behind schedule? Or will the Lions create the balanced game that keeps Chicago’s pass rush from taking over? Allen also offered a strong assessment of the group blocking for Gibbs. “This is probably the best offensive line that we faced to this point,” he said during his Monday media session . item.title: “Didn’t Feel So Special”: NCAA Champ Raises Questions About College Tennis After Title Win for Wake Forest Amid Absence of Top Players
item.description: Luca Pow - NCAA Men's Singles Champion | © Instagram /@lucapow_ & Instagram /@lta Luca Pow defeated fellow Demon Deacon Dominick Mosejczuk 7-5, 6-0 to claim the NCAA Division I men’s singles title at the University of Georgia on Sunday. It was Wake Forest’s first men’s tennis championship since Petros Chrysochos won in 2018. However, several top names were missing from the tournament: preseason No. 1 Dylan Dietrich, No. 2 Paul Inchauspe, No. 3 Duncan Chan, No. 4 Max Dahlin, No. 13 Mees Rottgering, and others withdrew from contention for a place in the conference Masters. After winning the NCAA championship, Pow was asked in his postgame interview whether the tournament lacked competition because several big names in collegiate tennis were absent. “Yeah, I mean, I spoke to [head coach Tony Bresky] a little bit after the match. I mean, it’s tough, you know. I felt that it didn’t feel as special because you don’t have the best guys in college here, but at the same time, you have to be in it to win it, right?” Pow said. “Everyone who’s competing and in college is here, and, yeah, it definitely didn’t feel so special, but obviously there’s so much history behind it, right? And that’s what makes it really special to me to be taking it home to Winston Salem,” he added. The 21-year-old Brit was one of three Demon Deacons to reach the tournament semifinals, highlighting the program’s dominance this year. The all-Wake Forest final also marked the first time since 2018 that players from the same program met in the championship match of the D1 tennis championships. Luca Pow Reflects On His Dominant NCAA Championship Run Pow dominated the field on his way to the national title. item.title: “Rob Better Have the Extension Ready,” “Best Pickup in Free Agency by Far”: Lakers Nation Showers Matisse Thybulle With Flowers Amid Historic Two-Way Surge
item.description: Matisse Thybulle © @Lakers/X Sometimes, it takes a change of scenery and system to reignite a player. That is exactly the case for Matisse Thybulle. He put up decent numbers as a role player for the Portland Trail Blazers but couldn’t make much of an impact, averaging 5.8 points in 30 games during the 2025-26 season. However, after joining the Lakers for the 2026-27 season on a one-year, veteran-minimum deal, Thybulle has returned to form with exponential improvement. In 17 games, he’s averaging 7.5 points while shooting 43.9% from the field, all as a starter. Not only has Thybulle taken over the starting role seamlessly, but he is also on pace to become the first Laker ever to average 2+ steals and 1+ block per game for a full season, while becoming a veteran presence for rookie guard Cameron Carr. During Monday’s 109-94 win over the Utah Jazz, he looked like one of the best players on the court. While Luka Doncic finished the game with 28 points, Thybulle had another strong performance on both ends. He finished with 14 points on 6-of-9 shooting, including 2-of-5 from deep. He added four rebounds, two steals, and two blocks in 27 minutes of action. Across the Lakers’ last three wins, he’s recorded 40 points, 13 rebounds and six steals. Fans had plenty of praise for the 3-and-D specialist, who was brought in as a depth piece before blossoming into an indispensable starter. Here is a look at some of their reactions: “Rob better have the extension ready,” one fan said. “He’s been awesome all season. Our best pickup in free agency by far,” another fan added. While many already knew he had this type of production in him, Thybulle has looked more confident compared to previous years. His physical presence and speed have also allowed him to make a real impact. As he continues to make a strong case for a spot in the Lakers’ starting lineup and a long-term payday, general manager Rob Pelinka has plenty of reason to consider locking him up before his price climbs even higher. Matisse Thybulle Receives Big Praise From Teammate Amid Historic Surge Matisse Thybulle’s strong play certainly grabbed the attention of Lakers forward Jake LaRavia, who had kind words for him after the game. “I know teams hate to see Matisse in the gap or in the passing lanes,” LaRavia said, as per @PurpGoldLakers via X. Seeing the Lakers so confident in Thybulle’s defense is certainly encouraging, and his energy has clearly resonated across the locker room. The Lakers undoubtedly have some very good players on their roster this campaign, and that is a big reason why they are 15-3, tied with the Spurs for the best record in the league. The Lakers now have three days of rest before facing the Spurs in a highly anticipated NBA Cup group-stage matchup on Friday. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
